correctness.rationale: For all integers m,n>=3, exact precedence constraints characterize every possible facet and explicit vertex orders realize all of them. The listed descending-cardinality pairings remove only free faces, never shared vertices, leaving a connected graph with 2mn vertices and 4mn-m-n edges. The equivariant Mayer-Vietoris sequence of the cover by contractible U_b and V_a is integral, has two generators for each two-point intersection, and gives the kernel module and full character, including the zero traces of exchanged cover and intersection terms under part swaps. An executable finite exhaustive verifier independently reconstructs all orders, tests 224 elementary collapses and 1,388 signed simplicial Lefschetz characters. These finite checks corroborate, not replace, the all-size proof.

value.rationale: The exact simple-homotopy classification applies to a natural two-parameter infinite family recently arising from strong discrete Morse theory. Despite arbitrarily high simplex dimension, all these complexes collapse to graphs; their fundamental groups, free integral homology and complete \(S_m\)×\(S_n\) first-homology representation are determined uniformly, with an additional balanced part-swap character. This extends the previously limited one-small-part calculation into a qualitatively different two-growing-part regime and supplies meaningful structural and equivariant information not implied by existing ordinary Morse complexes.
